title: HnswMetrics health metrics
wanted_capability: Expose neighbor-degree distribution, layer-occupancy stats, and recall diagnostics for HNSW indices.
evidence: crates/bbox-vectors/src/hnsw.rs:151-182 (metrics: avg degree, layer distribution, disconnected BFS)
gap-e2cb1ff8 (root-cause bug filed from these metrics)
notes: Partially shipped and proven useful: HnswMetrics now exposes avg_neighbor_degree, layer_distribution, and disconnected_nodes (BFS from entry point, semantics match search traversal) — these surfaced the prod 66,621/399,613 (~17%) disconnection that led to gap-e2cb1ff8 (add_reverse_edge orphaning, root cause confirmed by repro: zero in-degree accounts for disconnection exactly, 35% self-recall miss under large-cluster push order). Still missing from the original want: (a) in-degree distribution — the decisive diagnostic in the investigation (zero-in count pinpointed the mechanism); out-degree stats alone cannot see orphaning; (b) recall diagnostics — a sampled self-recall probe (search k=10 for indexed vectors, report miss rate) would have flagged this long before an operator eyeballed partition stats. Recommend closing this gap by adding those two to HnswMetrics alongside the gap-e2cb1ff8 fix, since the self-recall probe doubles as the fix's regression metric.
resolution_note: Closed alongside the gap-2eabd96d fix. HnswMetrics now exposes: avg_neighbor_degree + layer_distribution (shipped earlier), disconnected_nodes (BFS matching search semantics), and zero_in_degree_nodes (the in-degree diagnostic that attributed the orphaning exactly — zero_in == disconnected on every live measurement across both prod hosts). Recall diagnostics: self_recall_probe(sample_every, k) on HnswIndex gives sampled self-recall (used as the regression metric: 0.65 broken → 0.997 fixed at 20k scale). All surfaced through PartitionMetrics in hybrid_search vector_status. Not implemented from the original wishlist: a full neighbor-degree histogram — the zero-in count plus avg degree proved sufficient to diagnose the real incident; file a fresh gap if a histogram consumer appears.
